Colombian Automotive Firm Autovía S.A. Enters Liquidation Amid Cash Flow Crisis

Bogotá, June 21 — Colombian automotive manufacturer Autovía S.A. has entered court-ordered liquidation following a sustained period of financial distress, the company confirmed Thursday. The company, which has been a fixture in Colombia’s automotive sector for over three decades, cited mounting liabilities and constrained cash flows as key factors behind the move.

The process, supervised by Colombia’s Superintendence of Companies, has led Autovía to suspend production at its main assembly facility in Cundinamarca, resulting in immediate work stoppages for hundreds of employees. “This decision was not taken lightly, but it became unavoidable given the scale of our financial challenges,” said interim CEO Mauricio Londoño in a statement. All sales and after-sales operations have been halted pending further instructions from the liquidator. 

Industry analysts note that Autovía’s troubles reflect a tightening environment for domestic automotive producers, with a challenging macroeconomic backdrop and shifting consumer demand contributing to falling unit sales in recent quarters. “Autovía’s liquidation marks a significant moment for the sector, as it was one of the few remaining national manufacturers,” said Andrea Gutiérrez, an analyst at Bogotá-based consultancy Industria Movil.

The Colombian Automotive Industry Association (AICA) expressed concern for the workforce and the company’s legacy. “This is a sad day for the entire automotive community,” AICA said in a statement, urging authorities to support affected employees. The liquidation process is ongoing, with no timeline yet established for asset sales or possible restructuring. All operations at Autovía remain suspended as proceedings continue.
